works.title: Scaling Laws for Transfer (compute-efficiency halving)
works.why: Used to estimate how training costs fall over time due to algorithmic and hardware progress.

works.title: Scaling to Very Very Large Corpora for Natural Language Disambiguation
works.why: Cited as an early demonstration that more data eventually lets simple methods beat fancier ones ('the curves cross').

works.title: Large Language Models in Machine Translation
works.why: Cited as another case of simple scaled-up models eventually outperforming more complex rivals.

works.title: Six Challenges for Neural Machine Translation
works.why: Cited among the examples of neural methods eventually winning as data scales up.

works.title: Benchmarking scaling laws from literature-reported numbers
works.why: Criticized as a poorly controlled attempt to infer scaling laws from disparate papers, contrasted with the tightly controlled scaling papers.

works.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
works.why: Shows the smooth power-law curves relating loss to compute/data/parameters that the article uses to argue scaling keeps paying off.

works.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3 paper)
works.why: Reports GPT-3's size, training, and scaling results that the whole piece analyzes.

works.title: Measuring Systematic Generalization/Massive Multitask Language Understanding
works.why: Cited as another scaling curve showing model size versus question-answering performance.

works.title: Linguistic bias study of language models with scale
works.why: Cited as showing linguistic biases emerge more as training data increases.

works.title: On Robustness and Transferability of Convolutional Neural Networks (BiT robustness study)
works.why: Cited for showing transfer learning keeps improving even as raw classification accuracy plateaus.

works.title: Very Deep VAEs (deep variational autoencoders)
works.why: Cited as evidence that VAEs catch up to GANs/autoregressive models once made very deep.

works.title: NVAE: A Deep Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder
works.why: Cited alongside Child 2020 as evidence deep VAEs can match sharper image generators.

works.title: Soft-Robust Algorithms for Handling Model Misspecification (lottery-ticket/ensemble framing)
works.why: Cited for the idea that a big model encodes countless small sub-models, one of which solves the problem.

works.title: The Transition Between Overparametrization and Overfitting (double descent framing)
works.why: Cited regarding a possible phase transition where a model abruptly switches to a more abstract solution.

works.title: A Practical Guide to Sentiment Analysis (envisioned NLP eras figure)
works.why: Source of the figure depicting hypothetical S-curve eras of NLP progress used to frame the pretraining thesis.

works.title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch
works.why: Quoted on how much of English's entropy beyond simple n-gram models reflects grammar and world knowledge.

works.title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English
works.why: Cited for the classic estimate of English's entropy per character from human guessing experiments.

works.title: The Entropy of English Using PPM-based Models
works.why: Cited for a lower entropy estimate achieved using variable-length character n-gram models.

works.title: The Quiet Enemy (The Legacy of Hiroshima)
works.why: Source of the anecdote about Bohr's skepticism toward the atomic bomb being feasible, used as an analogy for skepticism about scaling.

works.title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling
works.why: Source of the 1 Billion Word benchmark used (and later excluded) in comparing GPT-2/GPT-3 perplexities to humans.

works.title: The Human Use of Human Beings
works.why: Quoted on how merely announcing a problem is solvable (as with the atomic bomb) spurs independent rediscovery, analogous to scaling.

works.title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
works.why: Cited as an early scaling paper from a Chinese-linked lab (Baidu) showing scaling predictability.

works.title: When Will Computer Hardware Match the Human Brain?
works.why: Source of the forecast that affordable compute for human-level AI would arrive in the 2020s, which the article says is being vindicated.

works.title: An Introduction to Wittgenstein's Tractatus
works.why: Source of the anecdote about heliocentrism feeling counterintuitive, used to argue a correct but counterintuitive view (agency in GPT-3) can still be right.

works.title: Story of Your Life
works.why: Cited as a fictional illustration of the variational/teleological way of describing a physical process as if it were goal-seeking.
